description: Nutritional profiles of millets, macro and micronutrient metrics, ingredient guidelines, and dietary facts.

fiber.significance: Millets possess significantly higher dietary fiber compared to polished white rice (0.2g) and refined wheat flour / maida (0.3g). Insoluble fiber adds digestive bulk and aids healthy bowel motility, while soluble fiber acts as a prebiotic fostering beneficial gut microbiota.
fiber.standout_millet: Barnyard Millet (up to 10.1% - 12g fiber) and Kodo Millet (9.8g).

protein.significance: Plant-based protein rich in essential amino acids (methionine, tryptophan, isoleucine, and leucine), crucial for tissue repair, cellular growth, and muscle recovery.

calcium.significance: Vital for bone density mineralization, teeth structure, blood clotting mechanisms, and nerve neurotransmission.
calcium.standout_millet: Finger Millet / Ragi (344 mg per 100g) — approximately 34 times higher than polished white rice (10 mg) and 10 times higher than wheat (30 mg).

iron.significance: Essential cofactor in hemoglobin synthesis and oxygen transport through red blood cells. Helps prevent iron-deficiency fatigue and anemia.
iron.standout_millet: Pearl Millet / Bajra (8.0 mg per 100g) and Little Millet (9.3 mg per 100g).

magnesium.significance: Supports over 300 biochemical reactions in the body, including cellular energy synthesis, vascular tone regulation, and insulin sensitivity.

ingredient_purity_principles: No refined wheat (Maida) or fillers in pure MilletVerse products.
Unrefined sweeteners preferred (organic jaggery, date paste, or raw honey) over high-fructose corn syrup or refined white sugar.
Cold-pressed oils or grass-fed cow ghee used in lieu of hydrogenated palm fats or trans-fat laden vegetable shortenings.
Zero artificial chemical preservatives, synthetic food colors, or emulsifying agents.
general_healthy_eating_guidance: Gradual Transition: Introduce millets gradually into your diet if you are new to whole grains, starting with 2-3 meals a week to allow gut microbes to adapt to the rich dietary fiber.
Adequate Hydration: Drink plenty of water throughout the day, as soluble and insoluble fiber requires adequate liquid to aid optimal digestion.
Balanced Plate: Pair millet dishes with wholesome legumes (dal, lentils, sprouts) and colorful vegetables for complete amino acid profiling and balanced nutrition.
Soaking Benefit: Soaking whole millet grains for 4 to 8 hours prior to cooking enhances mineral bioavailability and softens grain texture.
